summary: Reproduced nonlinear xgrammar 0.2.1 compilation cost for deeply nested JSON schemas and added a backend-independent, iterative serialized-JSON nesting guard before compiler dispatch. The guard also covers JSON schemas embedded in structural-tag payloads while preserving a measured 128-level object schema and non-JSON grammars.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the guard, actual xgrammar compilation completed depth 192 in 1.203s and depth 256 in 2.903s; depth 320 exceeded the 6s hard deadline and was killed. The listed exit code is the intentionally bounded depth-320 case.

84 tests passed, including failing-before/passing-after regressions proving excessive JSON nesting is rejected before backend dispatch, the boundary still dispatches, brackets in strings are ignored, structural tags are covered, and non-JSON grammars are unchanged.
The guarded implementation rejected depth 320 in 0.000677s, returned InvalidGrammarObject, and did not call the compiler dispatch.
A supported depth-128 object schema passed the guard and compiled with the actual xgrammar compiler in 0.356s.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-95de80bf7287/venv/bin/python -c '<ROCm 2x2 matrix multiplication and independent expected tensor comparison>'
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI355X with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015, GPU matrix multiplication returned [[19.0,22.0],[43.0,50.0]] with max absolute error 0.0 versus the independently specified expected tensor.

remaining_limitations: The external compiler API does not expose DFA/NFA state counts, so this change makes no unsupported state-count claim. It bounds the reproduced nesting vector before compilation. Very wide but shallow schemas remain subject to existing request-size controls and asynchronous grammar timeout behavior. No native source changed; source checkout was /job/repo and the prepared native artifact path was null.
